messages:
irene: Upgraded driver cluster-wide in eu-west at 00:05 UTC. After the rollout ~5% of H100 nodes are soft-failing — containers stuck in RUNNING but no progress. Anyone seeing this?

samir: Seeing same. NCCL errors spike around 00:12. Autoscaler started cordoning nodes and moving pods. Metrics: 12 failed jobs / 60m. Logs attached below.

infra-bot: ALERT: nodepool-eu-west-ml flapping: 12 evictions in 6m. link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/4621 :warning:

kevin: Paste dmesg from one affected host:
```
[ 1784.123456] nvidia 0000:04:00.0: failed to load kernel blob: kernel blob signature mismatch
[ 1784.123459] nvidia: driver=536.12, firmware=535.86
[ 1784.123461] nvlink: link error, reset requested
```
Looks like driver/firmware mismatch or SM90 kernel module failing to JIT.

maria: Can we binary-search the driver? Which hosts have the older firmware? Run:
```
ssh node-xx
nvidia-smi -q | grep -i firmware
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
```
If firmware < 536.0 then host GPU microcode needs update before driver bump.

noah: deploy-bot started a partial rollback by request from infra: rolling back to driver v535.86 on 4/5 canary hosts in eu-west-a. deploy id: db-2026-03-18-01

deploy-bot: Rollback started: image=ami-ml-eu-west:v20260317-driver53586 -> applied to 4 nodes. ETA 12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

samir: After rollback on canaries errors dropped ~90% on those nodes. However autoscaler still created new nodes in other regions as fallback — seeing cross-region jobs and >$4000/day egress estimate in the dashboard.

kevin: Root cause hypothesis: driver v536.12 requires updated GPU microcode and new NVLINK firmware; when host has old firmware the kernel driver refuses to load some SM90 kernels, causing NCCL timeouts and nvlink resets. Also our upgrade pipeline didn't run nccl-tests smoke.

maria: Short-term remediation:
- Pin driver minimum to v535.86 in baking AMIs for eu-west
- Disable auto-upgrades until we run a firmware rollout
- Add preflight: run `nccl-tests` + `nvlink check` + `nvidia-smi -q` on canaries

kevin: Long-term:
1) Add host-level check: compare `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` vs expected, fail upgrade if mismatch
2) Add NVLINK firmware check into image build
3) Canary schedule: rolling 1% -> 10% -> 50% with perf SLO gate
4) Update runbooks for SM90-specific driver/firmware matrix

irene: Agree. Can someone open an incident ticket and start a postmortem template? Also include cost impact so BD knows.

samir: Opening INC-2026-0940. Will collect logs, node lists, driver/firmware mapping, and add timeline. I'll attach sample `dmesg` and `nccl` traces.

maria: FYI - temporary mitigation: set env `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL` and `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` for affected pools to reduce nvlink-specific launches while we stabilize.

noah: Noted. I'll coordinate rollback completion and hold further driver promotions in eu-west until postmortem.

kevin: After postmortem we should add a smoke step to our CI: run `python infra/tools/nccl_smoke.py --model=bert` on every node type. If passes, proceed with driver promotion.

samir: TL;DR: driver bump caused incompat with GPU firmware/NVLINK -> NCCL errors -> autoscaler churn -> cross-region fallbacks -> cost spike. Rollback in progress and canary verification next.

irene: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
